narrative.overview: Documents are galleys on a working desk, not rows in a table. A saturated working blue owns the page; documents sit on proof-paper sheets that carry every piece of copy at full contrast. The arrangement this system refuses is the SaaS admin - left nav, card grid, coloured status badges - because it hides the only thing the reader came for: whether a document has become answerable, and what to do when it has not. Graft is self-hosted per company, so this screen is the only manual its readers get.
keyCharacteristics: Committed colour: the desk blue carries ~40% of the desktop viewport, as a field rather than an accent.
State is a sentence in the copy flow; the exact code is one disclosure away.
Exactly one alarm colour, spent only on a real failure.
No enclosure: rules, indentation and marginal marks group instead of cards and boxes.
One family of type; mono reserved for real data.

rules.name: The One Alarm Rule
rules.body: Correction red appears only where something actually broke: a failed document's marginal rule and state headline, and problem notices. Destructive actions take a dashed underline in ink, because deleting on purpose is not a failure.

rules.name: No Enclosure
rules.body: Nothing is grouped by putting a container around it. Rules, indentation and marginal marks carry structure; the only boxes are form controls, which are affordances.

rules.name: The Sheet Has Edges
rules.body: The working sheet is capped at 54rem. Without the cap the desk collapses into trim and the committed colour strategy dies.

rules.name: Translate, Don't Hide
rules.body: Plain language leads and the exact code is always reachable. Never remove the technical value; never let it lead.

dos: Do write every state as a sentence a non-technical reader understands.
Do give every failure a terminal state and a next action; stop polling and say so when nothing moves.
Do theme the browser's own surfaces: selection, caret, scrollbar, focus ring.
Do reserve mono for data that is actually data.
donts: Don't add a second alarm colour, or spend the red on emphasis or delete buttons.
Don't reach for a card, box or divider to group something.
Don't add status badges, chips or pills - that is the arrangement this system exists to refuse.
Don't introduce a display face; Operate mode is served by one well-tuned sans.
